continuation_evidence: INFERRED FROM ARITHMETIC; GSK states no footnote or sentence saying where Rukobia is reported from 2026. HIV table, Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1131399/000165495426004051/a2755c.htm): 'HIV | 1,824', 'Dolutegravir products | 1,295', 'Long Acting Injectables | 488', 'Other | 41 | (5) | (2)'; 1,295 + 488 + 41 = 1,824, so no further HIV row exists and Rukobia, no longer printed, can only sit in Other. Q2 2026 release: 1,441 + 593 + 44 = 2,078. Q1 2025 release printed 'Rukobia | 38' and 'Other | 5' (HIV 1,714; 1,824 against 1,714 is the printed +6%, so the HIV total is like for like); 1Q26 Other 41 at (5)% implies a base of about 43 = 38 + 5, and 2Q26 Other 44 at (15)% implies about 52 = 44 + 8. The row is a residual that also holds the products that were in Other before 2026; Rukobia's own share is not printed.

gold_notes: Immunex's MD&A product sales table (net product sales by product, USD millions; the Enbrel row). Enbrel sales began Nov. 4, 1998 (the 10-K: 'Sales of ENBREL commenced on November 4, 1998, and totaled $12.7 million for 1998'), so the full-year figure is all fourth-quarter sales and the first three quarters of 1998 had none (the Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 1998 lists no Enbrel sales). Enbrel product sales as Immunex recorded them: U.S. sales from the Nov. 4, 1998 launch, and U.S. plus Canada from the first quarter of 2001 (Immunex's 2001 Form 10-K states Enbrel was approved in Canada in December 2000 and became commercially available there in March 2001, and that Immunex records all Enbrel product sales in the U.S. and Canada). American Home Products owned Enbrel rights, and booked sales, outside the U.S. and Canada, so these are not worldwide sales.
revenue_scope: U.S. (1998Q4-2000Q4), U.S. and Canada (2001Q1-2002Q1); American Home Products had rights and booked sales elsewhere

continuation_evidence: Takeda Quarterly Financial Report for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2021 (https://assets-dam.takeda.com/raw/upload/v1662727335/legacy-dotcom/siteassets/system/investors/quarterly-announcements/fy2020/qr2020_q4_qfr_en.pdf), page 74, Q4 table: 'VELCADE *1 27.5 25.2 -8.4% 24.1 -8.6% 1.1 -3.5%' with footnote '*1 License-out product : Regional breakdown is not available due to contract.' geography: Takeda's total for the product: the table prints a US column and an ex-US column (Japan, EUCAN and GEM columns are blank for VELCADE). gold_notes: Takeda's own printed VELCADE line (total revenue of the product, JPY billions, one decimal; the table footnote reads 'License-out product : Regional breakdown is not available due to contract.'). Takeda's fiscal year runs April-March: FY2021 Q3 (October-December 2021) is mapped to calendar quarter 2021Q4. Current-quarter column of the quarter's own Quarterly Financial Report (Q3 table, page 66).
revenue_scope: Takeda's VELCADE row of the product revenue table in its Quarterly Financial Reports: the product's total revenue as Takeda reports it, JPY billions, with a US column and an ex-US column and no further regional split (footnote: 'License-out product : Regional breakdown is not available due to contract.'). Takeda holds VELCADE in the U.S.; J&J's gold series is J&J's own WW row, so the two lines are different scopes and different currencies.

why_separate: Takeda's gold series is its 'Nesina Japan' line, which Takeda labels NESINA-F and footnotes as including fixed dose combinations and blister packs; Teijin, which bought the Japan sales of Nesina, Liovel, Inisync and Zafatek from Takeda at the beginning of April 2021, prints Nesina alone and the combinations on their own rows. Pfizer prints a single Protonix row with no footnote separating brand from generic: its 2010Q1 value 158 compares with Wyeth's branded 86.966 and family total 237 for 2009Q2, so the row is not documented to be the branded-only scope. The owner also changed (Wyeth to Pfizer) and Pfizer renamed the line Protonix/Pantoprazole in 2014.
